title: The same average can hide a split
hook: Keep the aggregate unchanged while changing group heterogeneity.

doesNotKnow: Recognize that one mean cannot identify the underlying group distribution.

misconception: An aggregate rate of 50% means every subgroup is also 50%.
objective: Recognize that one mean cannot identify the underlying group distribution.

claims.text: Aggregate outcomes can conceal differences in how success is distributed.
Both mixtures give {A}% and {B}%. One separates high and low expected rates; the other gives both groups the aggregate rate.
Does it hold up? Rates are stipulated, not observed streaks. Equal averages establish neither equal randomness nor equal skill or individual outcomes.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: Equal groups average 60% overall. Must each group be 60%?
recall.why: 80% and 40% also average 60%; the aggregate cannot identify both group rates.
